children: The International Monetary Fund said on Wednesday that it had reached an agreement with Egypt to unlock a disbursement of about $2.3 billion in funds, subject to approval by the IMF's board, as the country nears the end of its $8 billion loan programme.
Egypt would receive about $1.5 billion under the IMF's 48-month loan programme after completing the final review, along with roughly $800 million under the Resilience and Sustainability Facility.

"The authorities’ successful implementation of their economic reform program and proactive response to the implications of the Middle East war have helped preserve macroeconomic stability and supported Egypt’s resilience in the face of a series of external shocks," the IMF said in a statement.
Egypt's programme with the IMF was expanded to $8 billion in March 2024, when ⁠the ​country was grappling with high inflation and foreign currency shortages.
Egypt's President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi has signaled that Egypt will not seek fresh IMF financing, directing officials to prepare a post-IMF “national programme".

The global lender said Egypt's economy remained resilient despite heightened regional tensions, with growth reaching 5.1% in the fiscal year ending June 2026, supported by a recovery in Suez Canal and petroleum-related activity and continued strength in manufacturing, tourism and communications.

The IMF warned that escalating regional conflicts and tighter global financial conditions could trigger capital outflows and raise borrowing costs, while high debt and financing needs remained key vulnerabilities.
The fund also stressed that exchange-rate flexibility should remain the first line of defence against external shocks, with interventions limited to containing excessive volatility.

Egypt raised interest rates, by 100 basis points, in October for the first time since March 2024, a move welcomed by the IMF as a commitment to price stability amid heightened international oil prices and uncertainty.
